speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your ear pain and earring difficulty post-tympanoplasty, could you tell me how long ago your surgery was performed and if you have any discharge or hearing changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any visible redness, swelling, or discharge at the earring site, and is the pain localized to the earlobe or deeper within the ear canal? I also need to know if you have any history of nickel or metal allergies.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the pain triggered by chewing on the right side, and do you experience any clicking sounds in the ear or difficulty moving your jaw? I suspect a temporomandibular joint disorder.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any tenderness when I press on the muscles in front of your ear or near your jaw joint, and do you experience any locking or clicking sensations when opening your mouth? I need to confirm if the pain is referred from the temporomandibular joint rather than the surgical site.

Given the shooting pain with eating and lack of jaw symptoms, I suspect Eustachian tube dysfunction or a recurrent perforation affecting the graft. I need to visualize the tympanic membrane to rule out surgical complications like re-perforation or granulation tissue.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the otoscopy is normal and jaw tenderness is absent, the shooting pain with eating suggests trigeminal nerve irritation or referred pain from the temporomandibular joint despite the lack of local signs. Could you describe if the pain radiates to your teeth or cheek, and do you have any history of bruxism or teeth grinding?
